key_insight: Block-triangular joint drifting turns standard one-step trajectory data into a one-step generative surrogate by preserving the current-state marginal while directly sampling the conditional next-state distribution.
engineering_relevance: This enables stochastic trajectory simulation with one model evaluation per time step, reducing runtime and avoiding auxiliary generative substeps compared with diffusion, flow, and distillation approaches.
method: Apply a projected drift field to the empirical joint distribution of consecutive states.
Use a block-triangular architecture so the first block keeps the current-state marginal unchanged.
Make the second block a direct sampler for the conditional distribution of possible next states.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments showing accurate marginal and trajectory-dependent statistics and favorable accuracy-cost tradeoffs versus deterministic, diffusion-, flow-, and distillation-based surrogates.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of observed trajectory pairs, since standard data provide only one realized next state per current state and may limit conditional-learning fidelity.
paper_title: One-Step Generative Surrogate Models via Block-Triangular Joint Drifting
